references.text: Previously, Aaron's staff was turned into a snake as a sign from God to Moses at the burning bush.
The immediate context where Aaron cast his staff before Pharaoh and it became a snake.
Egypt's magicians also repeated the first plague of blood with their secret arts.
The magicians also repeated the plague of frogs with their secret arts.
The magicians could not repeat the plague of gnats and acknowledged that this was God's finger.
The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the plague of boils.
Egyptian wise men and sorcerers who could not interpret Pharaoh's dreams.
Warning against false prophets who perform signs and wonders.
Paul mentions Jannes and Jambres, who opposed Moses, traditionally identified as these Egyptian magicians.
Jesus warns of false prophets who will perform great signs and wonders.
The beast from the earth performs great signs to deceive people.
Direct narrative and theological precursor: The transformation of staffs into snakes is a recurring motif that escalates from a private sign to a public confrontation.
